Subject: Snowflake -> BigQuery TCO & feasibility review

Hi team,

Attaching the first-pass TCO model for the potential migration from Snowflake to BigQuery (tco_model_2026-09-05.xlsx). High level thoughts:

- Estimated 18–24 month breakeven with current query/ingest profile. Main levers are long-term storage tiering (nearline), sustained discounts, and reserved slots vs on-demand compute.
- We left current Snowflake credits/partner discounts out to be conservative.
- Migration costs: estimated 12–16 weeks of engineering work + third-party migration assistance (quoted separately).

Ask: please review the TCO and call out (by EOD Monday) any place you think assumptions are off — particularly: compression ratios, egress, and expected sustained concurrency.

I also propose a short sync with Google (Ben Liu) and a migration consultant (Amit Shah) to validate assumptions and capture any Google promotional credits that could materially change the analysis. If we pursue, we should also get a counter from Snowflake (Priya) on committed discount + migration support.

Attachments: tco_model_2026-09-05.xlsx

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Data Platform

Hi Naomi / team,

Thanks for the invite — happy to join and help validate the model. I attached a preliminary GCP pricing quote (gcp_pricing_quote.pdf) and a short note on options that often change TCO materially:

- Committed use discounts (CUDs) + sustained use credits. If you can commit to a 1–3 year spend profile we can show meaningful unit-cost reductions.
- Flex slots vs flat on-demand: depends on predictability. For highly spiky workloads, a hybrid approach is usually best.
- Migration credits: we can often provide promotional credits for first-time migrations; I need to confirm amounts but expect something in the low six figures for an evaluation migration.

I'll come prepared on the call with a checklist to validate assumptions in the sheet and a rough SOW template. Proposed times: Tue 2026-09-09 10:00 or 15:00 PT.

Regards,
Ben Liu

Hi Naomi / team,

Appreciate the transparency. Before you move too far down the migration path, a few quick items from Snowflake that often shift the decision:

1) We can provide a structured renewal offer that includes a 15% discount on committed credits + a one-time migration assistance credit (we typically fund partner-led migration pilots).
2) Engineering effort estimates can be reduced if we include partner tooling for schema translation and SQL conversion — we have vetted partners who have done this 30–40% faster for customers with heavy VARIANT usage.
3) Query profiling: if you share a 7-day anonymized profile, our performance team can run a lift/shift simulation and give an apples-to-apples cost estimate on identical workloads.

I've attached a draft SOW outline for partner-assisted migration (sow_draft_v2.pdf). Happy to jump on the same call with Google to walk through the timeline and what Snowflake would cover under a competitive renewal.

Best,

Subject: Re: Snowflake -> BigQuery TCO & feasibility review

Thanks everyone — good discussion. Key takeaways and asks (action items below):

- TCO: current model shows ~20% lower unit storage cost on BigQuery assuming 3x compression; if we reduce compression assumption to 2x the breakeven pushes to ~30 months. Marissa will update the sheet with a sensitivity table.
- Migration effort & credits: Google indicates potential promotional credits (Ben) and a SOW; Snowflake is offering a 15% renewal discount + migration assistance (Priya) — these are roughly comparable when you include partner credits.
- Risk: SQL dialect, UDFs, and downstream BI connectors to Looker/Metabase. Connor, please run the Looker/Metabase connector smoke tests against an anonymized export to surface any immediate blockers.

Action items:
1) Marissa: update the TCO with 2x and 3x compression scenarios + sensitivity table (due Mon 2026-09-13).
2) Connor: run connector smoke tests and report blockers (due Mon 2026-09-13).
3) Karthik: get a line-item SOW and migration timeline from Amit; request firm promotional credit numbers from Ben.
4) I'll consolidate and present a recommendation to finance/exec by 2026-09-20.

Dropping the Drive folder here for reference: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cTCO

Naomi
